:question/problem: If $A=\begin{bmatrix}1 & 2 \\ -1 & 0\end{bmatrix}$, then $A^2=$
:question/worked-solution:
To find $A^2$, multiply $A$ by itself using row-by-column products:

$$
\begin{aligned}A^2 &= A\cdot A \\ &= \begin{bmatrix}1 & 2 \\ -1 & 0\end{bmatrix}\cdot \begin{bmatrix}1 & 2 \\ -1 & 0\end{bmatrix} \\ &= \begin{bmatrix}1\cdot1+2\cdot(-1) & 1\cdot2+2\cdot0 \\ (-1)\cdot1+0\cdot(-1) & (-1)\cdot2+0\cdot0\end{bmatrix} \\ &= \begin{bmatrix}-1 & 2 \\ -1 & -2\end{bmatrix}.\end{aligned}
$$

The exponent counts matrix factors; it does not square each entry.

$$
\begin{aligned}B^2 &= B\cdot B \\ &= \begin{bmatrix}1 & 1 \\ -1 & 2\end{bmatrix}\cdot \begin{bmatrix}1 & 1 \\ -1 & 2\end{bmatrix} \\ &= \begin{bmatrix}1-1 & 1+2 \\ -1-2 & -1+4\end{bmatrix} \\ &= \begin{bmatrix}0 & 3 \\ -3 & 3\end{bmatrix}.\end{aligned}
$$

Since $B^4=B^2\cdot B^2$, square the result:

:question/problem:
Consider the matrix $C=\begin{bmatrix}1 & -1 & 0 \\ 1 & 0 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & 1\end{bmatrix}$. Find the missing entries of $C^3$.
$C^3=$
{{field-1}}$-1${{field-2}}
{{field-3}}{{field-4}}$1$
$2$$1${{field-5}}
:question/worked-solution:
First compute $C^2$ by multiplying rows of $C$ by columns of $C$:

$$
\begin{aligned}C^2 &= C\cdot C \\ &= \begin{bmatrix}1 & -1 & 0 \\ 1 & 0 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & 1\end{bmatrix}\cdot \begin{bmatrix}1 & -1 & 0 \\ 1 & 0 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & 1\end{bmatrix} \\ &= \begin{bmatrix}1-1+0 & -1+0+0 & 0-1+0 \\ 1+0+0 & -1+0+1 & 0+0+1 \\ 0+1+0 & 0+0+1 & 0+1+1\end{bmatrix} \\ &= \begin{bmatrix}0 & -1 & -1 \\ 1 & 0 & 1 \\ 1 & 1 & 2\end{bmatrix}.\end{aligned}
$$

Now use $C^3=C^2\cdot C$:

$$
C^3=\begin{bmatrix}0 & -1 & -1 \\ 1 & 0 & 1 \\ 1 & 1 & 2\end{bmatrix}\cdot \begin{bmatrix}1 & -1 & 0 \\ 1 & 0 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & 1\end{bmatrix}=\begin{bmatrix}-1 & -1 & -2 \\ 1 & 0 & 1 \\ 2 & 1 & 3\end{bmatrix}.
$$

The five missing entries are obtained from these row-by-column products:

$$
\begin{aligned}(C^3)_{11} &= 0\cdot1+(-1)\cdot1+(-1)\cdot0=-1 \\ (C^3)_{13} &= 0\cdot0+(-1)\cdot1+(-1)\cdot1=-2 \\ (C^3)_{21} &= 1\cdot1+0\cdot1+1\cdot0=1 \\ (C^3)_{22} &= 1\cdot(-1)+0\cdot0+1\cdot1=0 \\ (C^3)_{33} &= 1\cdot0+1\cdot1+2\cdot1=3.\end{aligned}
$$
